publish-boundary-test.ref: server/killSwitchSharing.test.ts (13) + server/publishChokePoint.test.ts (13). socialPublish.ts changed in two ways and both are covered. (1) The kill-switch check was EXTRACTED to killSwitchBlockedPlatforms so igAutopost — an autonomous cron measured at 116 live posts in prod — could share the operator's emergency stop instead of bypassing it. killSwitchSharing.test.ts pins the guard's decisions (global / publishing / per-platform, the DENY audit record naming WHICH switch fired, and the deliberate fail-open when switch state is unreadable) AND pins that the extraction left publishToSocial behaviourally identical — including the partial-block case where one platform is stopped and the other still publishes, which is the behaviour most likely to be lost in an extraction. (2) A `link` field was added, because its absence was WHY nickActions.socialPost reached around the door to metaSocial.socialPost; pinned through to postToFacebook. publishChokePoint.test.ts holds the claim gates at contentAdmin.publishCarousel and nickActions.socialPost, and adds a structural sweep asserting no NEW file can import the low-level publishers — the part that makes it stick, since adStudio was fixed alone on 2026-07-25 and this identical defect survived on three other surfaces. Both structural assertions red-green verified: planting a file that imports postToInstagram fails the sweep by name; removing igAutopost's guard branch while keeping the call fails its pin. CADENCE IS NOT CLAIMED — this change deliberately did NOT apply the feed cap to igAutopost, because policy v7 sets maxFeedPostsPerDay=2 while the autoposter has been doing 3/day on 8 of the last 14 active days, and that conflict is the operator's to resolve, not this PR's to decide silently. PR #1127.

cron-fail-closed.ref: server/ros083ReviewQueue.test.ts (6), mutation-verified three ways. The cron file changed here is cron/jobs/reviewRequests.ts, and the change is a DIRECTION change on failure, so the fail-closed question is the right one to ask of it. BEFORE: the handler caught everything and returned { recordsProcessed: 0 }. Both runners record a RESOLVED handler as `completed` (cron/index.ts:218, cron/scheduler.ts:418) and log `failed` only when the handler THROWS — so an outage on the job that texts customers was filed in cron_log as a successful run that did nothing. AFTER: it re-throws. WHY THAT IS STILL FAIL-CLOSED, checked rather than assumed: (1) the throw happens BEFORE the send loop and before any row is claimed — getPendingReviewRequests is read up front, and claimReviewRequest (the atomic pending->sent claim) is only reached inside the loop, so no partial send and no half-claimed row is possible on this path; (2) neither runner retries a failed handler — grep for retry/attempt in cron/scheduler.ts and cron/index.ts finds no retry loop on the job path, so the job simply waits for its next 30-minute interval and a throw cannot re-fire it within the tick; (3) lock behaviour is UNCHANGED, which is the property that actually protects against duplicate SMS: scheduler.ts releases the lock in `finally` for both the resolved and the thrown path and withholds it only on TIMEOUT (timedOut stays false for a thrown error), so this change does not touch the zombie-handler protection at all; (4) the daily cap and quiet-hours gates are untouched. WHAT THE THROW BUYS: cron/observer.ts counts CONSECUTIVE `failed` rows per job and raises the job once it crosses its threshold, reading error_message. Under the old swallow this job could never produce a `failed` row, so it was structurally invisible to the failure observer no matter how long it had been broken. Also fixed in the same file: `recordsProcessed: typeof result === "number" ? result : 0` was never true — processReviewRequestQueue returns an object from all five of its exits and always has — so every run this job has ever made logged recordsProcessed: 0, including runs that sent real SMS; it now reports result.processed with a `details` string carrying the decline reason, so a legitimate zero (cap reached, quiet hours, gateway offline) is legible as a decision rather than as nothing happening. Mutations verified RED and each file restored byte-identical: re-swallowing in the catch turns 1 case red, restoring the typeof branch turns 1 case red, restoring the [] on getReviewRequests turns 1 case red. NOT CLAIMED: no live cron run and no prod cron_log observation — the assertions above about runner behaviour are read from cron/index.ts and cron/scheduler.ts, not measured against a deployed tick.

operator-walkthrough.ref: WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES, on a phone — /admin -> Outreach -> Review Requests, the page whose numbers authorise a batch of REAL outbound customer SMS. Reproducible with no production access: point DATABASE_URL at a dead host and open the tab. BEFORE: five tiles read "Total Requests 0 / Sent 0 / Clicked 0 / Click Rate 0% / Pending 0", the header read "0 review requests", the list read "No review requests yet — Requests are automatically created when bookings are marked as completed", and — this is the one that matters — tapping Process Queue opened a DANGER confirm dialog reading "currently ~0 due now". That number is the operator's only sanity check before firing the batch, and it was a measurement that had never been taken, presented as a reassuring one. AFTER: an amber strip over the tiles ("Review request stats could not be read... NOT zero"), em dashes on all five, the header reads "Review requests could not be read", the list is replaced by an amber block saying the queue is unknown and NOT empty, and the confirm dialog says the due count is UNKNOWN, is not zero, and may be a full batch. ★ THE PROCESS QUEUE BUTTON STAYS ENABLED, deliberately. The server is the authority on what is actually due; disabling the button would hide a queue that may be real and would train the operator to treat a greyed control as "nothing to do". What changes is that the dialog stops lying about the size of what it is about to send. ★ A SECOND, INDEPENDENT FAILURE, at the cron layer, fixed in the same change: cron/jobs/reviewRequests.ts caught every error and returned { recordsProcessed: 0 }. Both cron runners record a RESOLVED handler as a `completed` run (cron/index.ts:218, cron/scheduler.ts:418) and log `failed` only when the handler THROWS — so an outage on the job that texts customers appeared in the admin cron table as a successful run that happened to do nothing, indistinguishable from a genuinely drained queue. It now re-throws; the log.error stays for the local trace. ★ AND A THIRD, found while reading the second: `recordsProcessed: typeof result === "number" ? result : 0` was never true, because processReviewRequestQueue returns an object from all five of its exits and always has. This job has logged recordsProcessed: 0 into cron_log for every run it has ever made, INCLUDING runs that sent real SMS. The count was not low — it was not a count. It now reports result.processed, with a `details` string carrying the decline reason so a legitimate zero (cap reached, quiet hours, gateway offline) reads as a decision rather than as nothing happening. NOT FIXED, registered instead as ROS-084: getReviewSettings fabricates `enabled: 1` and getReviewRequestsSentToday fabricates `0` on the same outage — the daily-cap denominator and the operator's own off switch. Both point toward sending rather than holding. They are left alone because they change WHEN REAL SMS FIRE rather than what the admin sees, and that deserves its own review. EVIDENCE: server/ros083ReviewQueue.test.ts (6), MUTATION-VERIFIED THREE WAYS — restoring the [] read, re-swallowing in the cron catch, and restoring the typeof branch each turn exactly one case red, and every file was restored byte-identical (0 residual markers). DB-unavailable is induced by clearing DATABASE_URL, which is what getDb() actually branches on, rather than by mocking the export: getDb is defined inside db.ts and called through its local binding, so a module mock would not intercept the internal call sites and the test would have passed while exercising nothing. Full serial suite green (figures in the PR body). tsc --noEmit clean. NOT CLAIMED: no live production observation, and no assertion about how many SMS a real run sends. NOTE ON THIS KEY: last-writer-wins by design — the manifest lives on main while requirements are derived per-diff, so this text describes the most recently merged operator-facing change and nothing else.

capability-ledger-updated.deferred: No capability gains or loses a state, so no ledger entry is edited. The rule fires on one new file under server/services/**: reelReliability.ts. That file is a VERBATIM extraction of the getReelReliability body out of routers/instagramAdmin.ts — verified by diffing the logic lines, which are byte-identical; the only deltas are the `unknown` literal gaining an explicit ReelReliability annotation (same eight fields, same null values) and the sibling import path changing from ../services/reelRecoverability to ./reelRecoverability. The router now delegates in two lines. Nothing nickstire CAN DO changed: no new surface is exposed, no capability changes operationalState, no provider, cost, publish or generation path is touched, and the healthy path is behaviourally identical. The extraction exists so the admin console and the operator's phone read the SAME arithmetic instead of two copies that drift. The other two nickstire edits: (a) two READ-ONLY delegates added to the nour-os-query QUERY_HANDLERS map (instagram_delivery_issues, instagram_reel_reliability), each a one-line call into an existing service; (b) an ADDITIVE dbReadable:!!db field on the pre-existing instagram_autopost_status handler, so an unreadable log table can be told apart from an idle lane — additive because the other consumer of that query (statenour lib/ai/tools/social.ts) hands the raw result to an LLM and reads no specific field, so nothing can break. The operator-facing change is entirely on the statenour side (/ig Telegram commands), which this ledger does not track; the nearest entry, operator-command-center, describes the admin console and is unaffected. EVIDENCE: apps/statenour/tests/telegram/ig-format.test.ts (17) pins the rendering contract that null means UNKNOWN and never zero — an all-null ReelReliability renders 'UNKNOWN, not healthy' rather than '0 jobs', and dbReadable:false renders unknown rather than 'No autopost runs recorded'. Both verified by FALSIFICATION, not assumed: disabling each guard turns exactly the corresponding test red and leaves the compatibility test passing. nickstire: 22 test files / 333 passed / exit 0, including adminPermissionCoverage and bridge-shapes. statenour: 428 files / 4824 passed / 1 skipped / exit 0. NOT CLAIMED: the webhook wiring (igBridgeError / igRead / dispatch) has no direct test — that route has never had one and testing it needs prisma + journal-brain mocks. The rendering logic, where the risk lives, is fully covered. PR #1331.
